title: This Crane Lifts Itself Into the Sky
sources: HowStuffWorks 'How Tower Cranes Work' (p.3 'Why Don't Tower Cranes Fall Over?') / Heavy Equipment College 'How Do Tower Cranes Work?' / Scienceabc 'How Do Tower Cranes Work': the short counter-jib carries heavy concrete counterweight blocks that balance the load on the long working jib; the mast is bolted to a large concrete foundation pad (HowStuffWorks: about 400,000 lb)

HowStuffWorks 'How Much Weight Can Tower Cranes Lift?' / EP0667315B1 'Method and device to limit the load moment of a tower crane' / Maxim Crane 'Tower Cranes: Types, Parts, and How They Work': the further out the trolley carries a load, the less it may weigh; load-moment and max-load limiters stop the crane from exceeding its limits

HowStuffWorks 'How Do Tower Cranes Grow?' / Heavy Equipment College 'How Tower Cranes Are Put Together' / Astro Crane 'How Do Tower Cranes Work?' / US3485384A 'Method of climbing a tower crane': a climbing frame with hydraulic rams jacks the top of the crane up by one mast section (about 20 ft) and the crane lifts in a new mast section to fill the gap

UK HSE 'Tower crane slew brakes' safety bulletin / CPA TCIG TIN 038 / KHL 'Weather vane your tower crane for Hurricane Irene': when out of service the slew brake is released so the jib can turn freely with the wind (weathervaning) instead of resisting it

lines.text: If you hang a steel beam off the end of a long arm, the whole crane tips over.
lines.caps: If you hang a steel beam | off the end of a long arm, | the whole crane | tips over.

lines.text: So you stack giant concrete blocks on a short arm out the back.
lines.caps: So you stack giant | concrete *blocks | on a short arm | out the back.

lines.text: But all that weight presses down on one skinny steel tower.
lines.caps: But all that weight | presses down | on one skinny steel tower.

lines.text: So you bolt it to a concrete pad weighing around four hundred thousand pounds.
lines.caps: So you bolt it | to a concrete pad | weighing around | *400,000 pounds.

lines.text: But roll a heavy load too far out, and the balance is gone.
lines.caps: But roll a heavy load | too far *out, | and the balance is gone.

lines.text: So sensors weigh every lift, and stop the crane at the limit.
lines.caps: So *sensors weigh | every lift, | and stop the crane | at the limit.

lines.text: But the building keeps growing, until it's taller than the crane.
lines.caps: But the building | keeps growing, | until it's taller | than the crane.

lines.text: So the crane climbs itself. Hydraulic jacks push the whole top up about twenty feet,
lines.caps: So the crane | *climbs itself. | Hydraulic jacks push | the whole top up | about 20 feet,

lines.text: and it lifts in a new steel section to fill the gap.
lines.caps: and it lifts in | a new steel *section | to fill the gap.

lines.text: At night, they leave it free to spin, so it turns with the wind like a weathervane.
lines.caps: At night, they leave it | free to spin, | so it turns with the wind | like a *weathervane.

lines.text: You see, a crane never fights the weight or the wind. It balances them.
lines.caps: You see, a crane | never fights the weight | or the wind. | It *balances them.

lines.text: That's why the crane over your city points a different way every morning.
lines.caps: That's why the crane | over your city | points a different way | every *morning.
